\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}v$ is a shortest path\end{tabular}}}}\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(7+7\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Simply summing\end{tabular}}}}

By selecting
\varepsilon^{\prime}=\frac{3\cdot\varepsilon}{7}
, we get that:
3\cdot d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(7+3\cdot\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.
Hence, it emanates that
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.
∎

This indicates that for
\case
c in
Claim
6.10
:

Claim 6.10
.

If
\case
c holds then
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.

Proof.

Note that either
\case
d or
\notcase
d hold. We have shown
Claim
6.8
and
Claim
6.9
. Hence, we conclude that either way
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.
∎

Going back to
\case
b from
Claim
6.11
:

Claim 6.11
.

If
\case
b holds then
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.

Proof.

This follows by
Claim
6.7
and
Claim
6.10
.
∎

We have covered all sub-cases of
\case
a2. Hence we can prove
Lemma
6.12
:

Lemma 6.12
.

If
\case
a3 holds then
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.

Proof.

By
Claim
6.6
and
Claim
6.11
we conclude that
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.
∎

This indicates the end of our case-analysis. We have covered all three possible cases. We now move to our main theorem, stating both the correctness and runtime of
Algorithm
2
:

Theorem 6.13
.

Algorithm
2
computes a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{2.15135313}\cdot\log W}}\right)
time, for an arbitrary
\varepsilon>0
and weights of the set
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[W}}\right]\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0,\infty}}\right\}
.

Proof.

The correctness follows by the case analysis and
Lemma
6.2
,
Lemma
6.12
and
Lemma
6.3
. We consider the runtime. Initializing
d
takes
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2}}}\right)
time. Computing
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) for all vertices requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) by
Observation
2.2
. Computing the hitting set
S_{1}
(respectively,
S_{2}
) can be done deterministically in
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) by
Observation
2.1
. Computing
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{1},n^{\gamma}}}\right)
requires
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\gamma}}}\right)
time by
Observation
2.3
. Finding both pivots of each vertex and computing the distances to both pivots requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(m}}\right)
by
Observation
2.6
. Finding the edge set
E_{S_{1}}
(respectively,
E_{S_{2}}
) requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) by
Observation
2.7
.

By
Observation
2.1
the size of
S_{1}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1-\beta}}}\right)
and the size of
S_{2}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1-\beta-\gamma}}}\right)
. By
Observation
2.5
the size of
E_{S_{1}}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
and the size of
E_{S_{2}}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
. As there are
n
vertices, the size of
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n}}\right)
, which is smaller than any
E_{S_{i+1}}
. Implementing the SSSP invocation by Dijkstra, the runtime will therefore be
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|S_{0}}}\right|\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|E_{S_{1}}}}\right|+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|S_{1}}}\right|\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|E_{S_{2}}}}\right|}}\right)=\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\beta}+n^{2+\gamma}}}\right)
. Recall that
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|S_{2}}}\right|\in\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1-\beta-\gamma}}}\right)
. Invoking the
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-MSASP from
S_{2}
requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(m^{1+o\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
.

Additional operations require:
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|E}}\right|\cdot n^{\beta}\in\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(mn^{\beta}}}\right)
time for the updates in the for-loop straight after the initialization;
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\gamma}}}\right)
time for the updates through
s\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{1},n^{\gamma}}}\right)
;
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2}}}\right)
for the final updates through all the pivots of either
u
or
v
.

This concludes the runtime cost of each operation. The total runtime is therefore
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\beta}+n^{2+\gamma}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
. We can
[
8
]
select
\beta=\gamma\approx 0.15135313
. Hence the runtime will be:
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{2.15135313}\cdot\log W}}\right)
.

To address the sparse case, we can slightly adjust the algorithm to depend on the graph’s density. Instead of simply considering
S_{1}
, we let
S_{1,1}\supseteq S_{1,2}\supseteq\ldots\supseteq S_{1,t}
for
t\in O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\log n}}\right)
. These sub-sets would actually be hitting-sets to the sets
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\frac{i\cdot\beta}{t}}}}\right)
for
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[t}}\right]
. This would result in reducing the runtime for the initial SSSP invocations from all
s\in S_{0}=V
.

Instead of invoking SSSP over the edges of
E_{S_{1}}
, we would invoke SSSP from all
s\in S_{1,i}
over
E_{S_{1,i+1}}
. The runtime for each of the
\log n
invocations would be
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2}}}\right)
instead of the previous single invocation which required
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\beta}}}\right)
.

We observe that the first for-loop iteration, right after the initialization, would still require
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(mn^{\beta}}}\right)
. This reduces the component of
n^{2+\beta}
to
mn^{\beta}
. As we still update through
s\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{1},n^{\gamma}}}\right)
our runtime still consists of the component of
n^{2+\gamma}
. Hence, repeating this idea for
S_{2}
would not result in any runtime improvement. The runtime now becomes
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(mn^{\beta}+n^{2+\gamma}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
instead of
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\beta}+n^{2+\gamma}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
.
∎

Multiplicative
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP

In this section we present
Algorithm
3
which is a framework of algorithms for
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP problems, where
\ell\in\mathbb{N}
. We observe that this is both a generalization of
Algorithm
2
, which is a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{7}{3}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP algorithm, and also a runtime improvement, for dense graphs, of the framework of
\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP algorithms presented by Akav and Roditty
[
3
]
.

The runtime of
Algorithm
3
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(mn^{\beta_{1}}+\msum{n^{2+\beta_{i}}}{i=2}{\ell+1}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\alpha_{\ell+1}}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
.
The previously mentioned parameter
\ell
indicates the trade-off between the runtime and the multiplicative stretch, while the values of the parameters
\beta_{1},\ldots,\beta_{\ell+1}\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(0,1}}\right)
will depend on graph’s density, and will be set during the runtime analysis of
Algorithm
3
.

Our algorithm works as follows: for
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]
we set
\alpha_{i}=\msum{\beta_{j}}{j=1}{i}
and compute a hitting set
S_{i}
to the sets
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\alpha_{i}}}}\right)
, over all
u\in V
. We compute the corresponding
E_{S_{i}}
. We also set
S_{0}=V
and
S_{\ell+2}=\varnothing
, hence
E_{S_{\ell+2}}=E
. We initialize the distance approximation matrix
d:V\times V\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}
to hold all edges’ weights or
\infty
else. We find the pivot
p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
for all
u\in V
and update the distance
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]\leftarrow\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
by a single SSSP invocation (See:
Observation
2.6
).

Following the initialization, we update the distances, for
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]
, from any
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x,y}}\right)\in E
to
p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)
of
v\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y,S_{i-1},n^{\beta_{i}}}}\right)
. That is,
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),x}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),v}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[v,y}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[x,y}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),x}}\right]}
. We now consider an
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0}}\right\}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell}}\right]
and proceed with an SSSP invocation from all
s\in S_{i}
over the weighted graph
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(s}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E_{S_{i+1}}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H,d}}\right)
, where:

\blacklozenge

E_{S_{i+1}}
- The union, over
all

u\in V
, of edges
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
such that
w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)<\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{i+1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
,

\blacklozenge

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V
- Auxiliary edges from
s
to
V
, representing distances previously computed,

\blacklozenge

H=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{j}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)\,\middle|\,\,u\in V}}\right\}
- Auxiliary edges from
any

u
to its pivots
p_{j}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
for
j\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]
.

The weight of each is given by
d:V\times V\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}
. Observe that
d
is a weight function over
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(s}}\right)
. We then proceed by a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-MSASP invocation from the set of sources
S_{\ell+1}
over the entire graph. We stress that, contrary to
Algorithm
and similarly to
Algorithm
2
, the order of invocations of SSSP and MSASP here holds no importance.

Finally, we apply two types of distance updates. Let
u,v\in V
and
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]
. First,
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,s}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[s,v}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]}
through any
s\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{i},n^{\beta_{i+1}}}}\right)
. The second is from all the
2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)
pivots
13
13

13

Recall that
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]
is updated whenever
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[v,u}}\right]
is updated.
of both
u
and
v
, namely:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]}
.

To prove the correctness of our algorithm, we follow an analogous proof to the
\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP of Akav and Roditty
[
3
]
. As we performed changes to their algorithm, we provide a full proof of
Algorithm
3
, indicating where the additional
\varepsilon
affects.

We begin with
Claim
7.1
, where we state certain properties, which remind us of the properties of the edge
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x,y}}\right)
stated in
Lemma
6.1
in
Section
6
.

Input:
An undirected graph

, a positive weight function

, an integer

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP.

Let

to be fixed later

Initialize

as the edges’ weights and
\infty
otherwise

for

do

\alpha_{i}\leftarrow\msum{\beta_{j}}{j=1}{i}

for

do

\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{i},n^{\beta_{i+1}}}}\right)

Compute the distances from any

to its pivot

Construct the set of edges

for

do

for

do

for

for

do

for

and update

accordingly

Compute a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-MSASP from

on

and update

accordingly

for

u,v\in V

do

for

do

for

. As

, it follows that:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right]\leq 2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
. By a symmetric argument for

, we can show that:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),v}}\right]\leq 2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
. By the selection of the index
i
it follows that:

2d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq 2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)+2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right)\leq 4\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)

It follows that

It follows that there is only a single edge
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)\notin E_{S_{i+1}}
. If either

or

it would contradict
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)\notin E_{S_{i+1}}
. The same contradiction would occur if
a\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
or
b\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
. As either vertex must be within
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
or
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
, it follows that
a\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
and
b\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
.

We briefly observe that
i<\ell+1
. Indeed, since
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)\notin E_{S_{i+1}}
, it must be that
E_{S_{i+1}}\neq E
. As
E=E_{S_{\ell+2}}
, it follows that
i+1<\ell+2
or
i\leq\ell
.
∎

Having proven the properties of the index
i
and the edge
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)
, we can now
establish two upper-bounds for
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]
. Combining them would result in the overall approximation. We begin with the first upper-bound:

Lemma 7.2
.

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mmin{3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,v}}\right),3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)}

Proof.

By
Claim
7.1
we know that
i\leq\ell
. Hence, as
E_{S_{\ell+2}}=E
, there exists an index
i+2\leq j\leq\ell+2
such that
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)\in E_{S_{j}}
. Therefore,
a\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,n^{\alpha_{j-1}}}}\right)
. As we may increase
j
or we have reached
j=\ell+2
, we may assume that
j
is the smallest index for which both
b\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,n^{\alpha_{j-1}}}}\right)
and
a\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,n^{\alpha_{j-1}}}}\right)
.

Consider
p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a}}\right)
and
p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b}}\right)
. Since
i<\ell+1\leq j-1
and
j
is the smallest index for which
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,n^{\alpha_{j}}}}\right)
then
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,n^{\alpha_{j-1}}}}\right)
which means that
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a}}\right)}}\right)\leq w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)
. Symmetrically,
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b}}\right)}}\right)\leq w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)
. Therefore:

\displaystyle\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)

. Consider two possibilities:
j<\ell+2
or
j=\ell+2
.

If
j<\ell+2
then
j-1\leq\ell
, hence
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
and
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),u}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right)
. If
j=\ell+2
then we invoked a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-MSASP from
S_{j-1}=S_{\ell+1}
, hence:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)}}\right)
and
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),u}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right)}}\right)
. In any case, as we consider both

and
p_{j-1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)

Before proceeding to the next bound, we direct the reader to
Appendix
B
, where we present the algorithm of Thorup and Zwick
[
27
]
, denoted as
Algorithm
7
. The correctness of the following bound relies on certain properties of
Algorithm
7
.

Lemma 7.3
.

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
or
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,v}}\right)

Proof.

Let
r\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[i}}\right]
be the largest index such that
a\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\alpha_{r}}}}\right)
and
u\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,n^{\alpha_{r}}}}\right)
. Let
q\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[i}}\right]
be the largest index such that
b\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,n^{\alpha_{q}}}}\right)
and
v\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,n^{\alpha_{q}}}}\right)
. By
Claim
7.1
it follows that
a\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
and
b\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,n^{\alpha_{i+1}}}}\right)
. Hence,
r,q<i+1
.

We distinguish between two cases. At first, we consider when
q\leq r
and show that
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)}}\right)
. For the second case, when
r<q
, we show that
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,v}}\right)}}\right)
. As the proof for the second case is symmetrical, we omit the details. We therefore focus solely on the case where
q\leq r
.

Before we continue, let us consider several edge cases. If

7
. Let

is odd,

is even and
f
is even.

f-r
is even as well. By
Lemma
B.1
it follows that
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f-r}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{r}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
. By the definition of
f

p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,S_{f},n^{\alpha_{f+1}}}}\right)

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)

Recall that we update
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]
to pass through
p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
. Ergo:

\displaystyle d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right]}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Update through $p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)$\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Our preceding inequality\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f-r}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{r}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Our pre-preceding discussion\end{tabular}}}}

If
r=0
then
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{r}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)=0
. As
f-r\leq\ell+1
it follows that:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
. If
r\geq 1
then
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{r}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
, as
r
was selected such at
a\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\alpha_{r}}}}\right)
. Therefore:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f-r+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
. Yet
r\geq 1
, hence:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot f\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
.

The rest of the proof, for the other parity cases, remains precisely as is in the proof of

]. As we make no changes, we omit the technical details for these cases.

Having proven both upper-bounds, we can now follow with our main theorem:

Theorem 7.4
.

Let
\alpha_{j}=\msum{\beta_{i}}{i=1}{j}
,
\varepsilon>0
with weights from
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[W}}\right]\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0,\infty}}\right\}
.
Algorithm
3
computes a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\alpha_{\ell+1}}}\right)}\cdot\log W+mn^{\beta_{1}}+\msum{n^{2+\beta_{i}}}{i=2}{\ell+1}}}\right)
time.

Proof.

By
Lemma
7.3
it follows that either
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
or
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,v}}\right)
. Assume, w.l.o.g., that:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
.

Due to
Lemma
7.2
we know that:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mmin{3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,v}}\right),3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)}
. Substituting the above yields that:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mmin{\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right),\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)}}\right)}
. We consider the following two possibilities:

1.

When
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)\leq\frac{\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)}{\ell+2}
. Then:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\frac{\ell+1}{\ell+2}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)=\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
,

2.

Otherwise:
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)>\frac{\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)}{\ell+2}
, or
-\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)<-\frac{\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)}{\ell+2}
. Therefore:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)}}\right)<\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)-\frac{2\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)}{\ell+2}}}\right)=\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}+\varepsilon\cdot\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.

By selecting
\varepsilon^{\prime}=\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+2}}\right)\cdot\varepsilon}{3\ell+4}
, we conclude the correctness of
Algorithm
3
.

We now turn to consider its runtime. Initializing
d
takes
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2}}}\right)
time. Let

. Computing

for all vertices requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\alpha_{i}}}}\right)
by

2.2
. Computing the hitting set

Algorithm 4

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon,\mmin{2W_{1},4W_{2}}}}\right)
-APASP
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(G=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E,w}}\right)}}\right)

In this section we introduce
Algorithm
4
, which considers on two parameters
\beta,\gamma\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(0,1}}\right)
, whose values will be determined when we will analyze the runtime.

Algorithm
4
proceeds as follows: we compute the hitting set
S_{1}
(resp.
S_{2}
) for the sets
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta}}}\right)
(resp.
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
), over all
u\in V
. We then compute the set
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{1},n^{\gamma}}}\right)
. We compute
E_{S_{1}}
(resp.
E_{S_{2}}
). We also set
S_{0}=V
and
S_{3}=\varnothing
.

The distance approximation matrix
d:V\times V\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}
is initialized to the weight of the edges or
\infty
else-wise. We find the pivots
p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
(resp.
p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
) for all
u\in V
and the exact distance
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]\leftarrow\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
(resp.
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]
) by a single SSSP invocation (See:
Observation
2.6
).

We proceed by invoking a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-MSASP from
S_{2}
over the entire graph. We then compute a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-AMPMM of
d_{0}^{2}\star d_{2}^{0}
, where
d_{i}^{j}
is a rectangular matrix containing all values of
d
, its rows narrowed down to include only the vertices of
S_{i}
and its columns to those of
S_{j}
. We note that similarly to
Algorithm
, the order here is of importance.

The following occurs twice, in decreasing order
i\leftarrow 1
to
0
(only two hitting sets): we perform an SSSP invocation from all
s\in S_{i}
on the graph
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(s}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E_{S_{i+1}}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H,d}}\right)
, where:

\blacklozenge

E_{S_{i+1}}
- The union, over
all

u\in V
, of edges
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
such that
w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)<\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{i+1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
,

\blacklozenge

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V
- Auxiliary edges from
s
to
V
, representing distances previously computed,

\blacklozenge

H=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{j}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)\,\middle|\,\,u\in V}}\right\}
- Auxiliary edges from
any

u
to its pivots
p_{j}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
for
j\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{1,2}}\right\}
.

In other words, after we performed an SSSP invocation from all
s\in S_{1}
, we perform one from all
v\in S_{0}=V
, then again from all
s\in S_{1}
and then finally one more time from all
v\in S_{0}=V
. We observe that
d:V\times V\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}
is a weight function over
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(s}}\right)
.

We then compute another
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-AMPMM, this time for the rectangular matrices
d_{0}^{1}\star d_{1}^{1}
. Finally, we perform one more SSSP invocation from all
u\in V=S_{0}
over the graph
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E_{S_{1}}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{u}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H,d}}\right)
.

To prove the
near additive
approximation of
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon,\mmin{2W_{1},4W_{2}}}}\right)
, we begin by presenting a case analysis in a case-tree, as we previously did for
Algorithm
2
.

and

. It might be that
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1},y_{1}}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{2},y_{2}}}\right)
. However,
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(z,t}}\right)\neq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1},y_{1}}}\right),\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{2},y_{2}}}\right)
by
\case
b2.

w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(z,t}}\right)\leq w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{2},y_{2}}}\right)

w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(z,t}}\right)\leq w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)
. Hence, we follow a similar argument as in
Lemma
8.5
.

:
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(t}}\right),u}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(t}}\right),u}}\right)

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(t}}\right),v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(t}}\right),v}}\right)
. Therefore:

After the second SSSP we compute
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-AMPMM for
d_{0}^{1}\star d_{1}^{1}
. Consider
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1}}}\right)}}\right]
and
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1}}}\right),p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y_{2}}}\right)}}\right]
. Therefore:

\displaystyle d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y_{2}}}\right)}}\right]

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1}}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1}}}\right),p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y_{2}}}\right)}}\right]}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}$\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)$-AMPMM for $d_{0}^{1}\star d_{1}^{1}$\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,x_{1}}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1},p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1}}}\right)}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1},p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1}}}\right)}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1},y_{2}}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y_{2},p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y_{2}}}\right)}}\right)}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}By the preceding discussion\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+4\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Because $\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(z,t}}\right)$ is heavier than both\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+4\cdot\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+4\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}$w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)$\end{tabular}}}}

We conclude by selecting
\varepsilon^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon}{4}
. This means that if
w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(z,t}}\right)\leq w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{1},y_{1}}}\right)

w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(z,t}}\right)\leq w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{2},y_{2}}}\right)
we can upper-bound our approximation by
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)
. Otherwise, we can provide two upper-bounds:
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right)
and
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+4\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)
. Hence, the actual upper-bound is
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\mmin{2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(a,b}}\right),4\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)}
.

∎

We are left with:

Lemma 8.5
.

If
\case
b3 holds then
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}v$ is a shortest path\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+2\cdot\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x_{2},y_{2}}}\right)}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Due to \case{b}{3}\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+2\cdot\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Our w.l.o.g. assumption\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+4\cdot\varepsilon+2\cdot\varepsilon^{2}}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}$w\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(c,d}}\right)\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)$\end{tabular}}}}

By selecting
\varepsilon^{\prime}=\sqrt{1+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}}-1
we complete the proof.
∎

This indicates the end of our case-analysis. Having covered all possible cases of our case-tree, we can now prove:

Theorem 8.6
.

Algorithm
4
runs in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{2.15135313}\cdot\log W}}\right)
time and computes a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon,\mmin{2W_{1},4W_{2}}}}\right)
-APASP, for weights of the range
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[W}}\right]\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0,\infty}}\right\}
.

Proof.

The correctness follows by the case analysis and
Lemma
8.1
to
Lemma
8.5
. Let us analyze the runtime. Initializing
d
takes
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2}}}\right)
time. Computing
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) for all vertices requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+2\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+2\beta+2\gamma}}}\right)
) by
Observation
2.2
. Computing the hitting set
S_{1}
(respectively,
S_{2}
) can be done deterministically in
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) by
Observation
2.1
. Finding both pivots of each vertex and computing the distances to both pivots requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(m}}\right)
by
Observation
2.6
. Finding the edge set
E_{S_{1}}
(respectively,
E_{S_{2}}
) requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) by
Observation
2.7
.

By
Observation
2.1
the size of
S_{1}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1-\beta}}}\right)
and the size of
S_{2}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1-\beta-\gamma}}}\right)
. By
Observation
2.5
the size of
E_{S_{1}}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta}}}\right)
and the size of
E_{S_{2}}
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1+\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
. As there are
n
vertices, the size of
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n}}\right)
, which is smaller than any
E_{S_{i+1}}
. Implementing the SSSP invocation by Dijkstra, the runtime will therefore be
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|S_{0}}}\right|\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|E_{S_{1}}}}\right|+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|S_{1}}}\right|\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|E_{S_{2}}}}\right|}}\right)=\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\beta}+n^{2+\gamma}}}\right)
. Recall that
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left|S_{2}}}\right|\in\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{1-\beta-\gamma}}}\right)
. The
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-MSASP invocation requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(m^{1+o\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
.

The first
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-AMPMM of
d_{0}^{2}\star d_{2}^{0}
requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
by the
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-AMPMM algorithm of Zwick
[
33
]
. Similarly, the second
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon}}\right)
-AMPMM invocation, this time of
d_{0}^{1}\star d_{1}^{1}
, requires
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1,1-\beta,1-\beta}}\right)}\cdot\log W}}\right)
. Repeating the same SSSP invocations twice or trice does not add to the overall runtime.

The total runtime is therefore
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\beta}+n^{2+\gamma}+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1-\beta-\gamma}}\right)}+n^{\omega\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1,1-\beta,1-\beta}}\right)}}}\right)\cdot\log W}}\right)
. We
[
8
]
select
\beta=\gamma\approx 0.15135313
. Hence the runtime will be:
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{2.15135313}\cdot\log W}}\right)
.
∎

This concludes the correcness and runtime analysis of
Algorithm
4
.

Multiplicative and additive trade-offs

We recall that
Algorithm
computed a
+2\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}
-APASP and
Algorithm
6
by Akav and Roditty
[
3
]
computed a
\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP (See:
Appendix
B
). For dense graphs, where
m\in\tilde{\Theta}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2}}}\right)
, the latter is a
\frac{9k+4}{3k+2}
-APASP algorithm with
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{3k+2}}}}\right)
runtime, by setting
\ell=3k
.

Claim 9.1
.

Let
\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{+}
. It is possible to compute a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(9k+4}}\right)\cdot\alpha+\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3k+2}}\right)\cdot\beta}{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\alpha+\beta}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3k+2}}\right)},\frac{2\beta}{\alpha+\beta}\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}}}\right)
-APASP in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{3k+2}}}}\right)
time.

The proof is straightforward:

Proof.

Let
k\in\mathbb{N}
. Invoke both
Algorithm
and
Algorithm
6
, the latter for
\ell=3k
. The runtime of
Algorithm
is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{3k+2}}}}\right)
due to
Theorem 5.3
. The runtime of
Algorithm
6
is at most
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{\ell+2}}}}\right)=\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{3k+2}}}}\right)
(for details, see
Appendix
B
). Hence, their total runtime remains
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{3k+2}}}}\right)
.

Invoking both algorithms guarantees us that:

1.

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}
,

2.

and
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\frac{9k+4}{3k+2}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)
.

By considering any
\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{+}
, we can simply average these upper-bounds:

\displaystyle\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\alpha+\beta}}\right)\cdot d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\alpha\cdot\frac{9k+4}{3k+2}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+b\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\beta\cdot\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Summing both upper-bounds\end{tabular}}}}

\displaystyle\leq{\underbrace{\frac{\alpha\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(9k+4}}\right)+\beta\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3k+2}}\right)}{3k+2}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\beta\cdot\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}}_{\mbox{\scriptsize\begin{tabular}[]{@{}c@{}}Simply summing\end{tabular}}}}

Dividing by
\alpha+\beta
, we conclude that:

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\frac{\alpha\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(9k+4}}\right)+\beta\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3k+2}}\right)}{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\alpha+\beta}}\right)\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(3k+2}}\right)}\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\frac{2\beta}{\alpha+\beta}\cdot\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}

∎

We observe that
Claim
9.1
partially addresses
Question
5
, by presenting a family of APASP algorithms computable in
\tilde{O}(n^{2+\frac{1}{3k+2}})
time.
Claim
9.1
also partially answers
Question
4
, as, when
\alpha=\beta=1
, we get a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{6k+3}{3k+2},\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}}}\right)
-APASP, whose multiplicative stretch is smaller than
2
. For instance,
k=1
indicates that a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{9}{5},W_{1}+W_{2}}}\right)
-APASP can be computed in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{\frac{11}{5}}}}\right)
.

The same idea can be applied as well to
Algorithm
3
that computed a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}+\varepsilon}}\right)
-APASP and the
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1+\varepsilon,2\msum{W_{i}}{i=1}{k+1}}}\right)
-APASP algorithm of Saha and Ye
[
23
]
, e.g. a
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{5}{3}+\varepsilon,\mmin{W_{1},2W_{2}}}}\right)
-APASP computed in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}\right)^{O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(1}}\right)}\cdot n^{2.15135313}\cdot\log W}}\right)
time.

For completeness, we provide values for the
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\alpha,\beta}}\right)
-APASP examples where
\alpha\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(2,\frac{7}{3}}}\right)
that were mentioned in
Section
1
between
Question
4
and
Question
5
. Consider the following:

\blacklozenge

\alpha=3
,
\beta=1
and
k=1
results in
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{11}{5},\frac{W_{1}+W_{2}}{2}}}\right)
-APASP in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{\frac{11}{5}}}}\right)
time;

\blacklozenge

\alpha=2
,
\beta=1
and
k=2
results in
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{13}{6},\frac{2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(W_{1}+W_{2}+W_{3}}}\right)}{2}}}\right)
-APASP in
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{\frac{17}{8}}}}\right)
time.

Appendix A
Multiplicative
\frac{7}{3}
-APASP

Input:
An undirected graph
G=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E}}\right)
and a positive weight function
w:E\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}
.

Output:
A matrix
d
which is a
\frac{7}{3}
-APASP.

Let
\beta,\gamma\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(0,1}}\right)
to be fixed later

Initialize
d
as the edges’ weights and
\infty
otherwise

Compute
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\beta}}}\right)
(respectively,
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
) for all
u\in V

Compute
S_{1}
(respectively,
S_{2}
) to be a hitting set to
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\beta}}}\right)\mid u\in V}}\right\}
(respectively,
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\beta+\gamma}}}\right)
)

Compute the distances from any
u\in V
to its pivot
p_{1}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
(respectively,
p_{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)
)

Construct the set of edges
E_{S_{1}}
(respectively,
E_{S_{2}}
)

for

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x,y}}\right)\in E

do

for

v\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y,V,n^{\beta}}}\right)

do

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0,1,2}}\right\}

do

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),x}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),v}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[v,y}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[x,y}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),x}}\right]}

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0,1,2}}\right\}

do

for

s\in S_{i}

do

Invoke SSSP from
s
on
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(s}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E_{S_{i+1}}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H,d}}\right)
and update
d
accordingly

for

u,v\in V

do

for

s\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{1},n^{\gamma}}}\right)

do

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,s}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[s,v}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]}

for

u,v\in V

do

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[1,2}}\right]

do

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]}

return

d

Algorithm 5

\frac{7}{3}
-APASP
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(G=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E}}\right),w}}\right)

For completeness, we present a simplified version of the
\frac{7}{3}
-APASP algorithm of Baswana and Kavitha
[
6
]
. Instead of
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(nm^{\frac{2}{3}}+n^{2}}}\right)
time, the runtime for the simplified version is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{\frac{7}{3}}}}\right)
. The main difference between our versions lies in
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\beta}}}\right)
. While we considered only this set, Baswana and Kavitha considered, for
t\in O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\log n}}\right)
, the sub-sets leading to it. Namely these are:
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\frac{i\cdot\beta}{t}}}}\right)
, for
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[t}}\right]
. This results in
t
hitting-sets
S_{1,1},S_{1,2},\ldots,S_{1,t}
. The runtime then reduces to
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(nm^{\frac{2}{3}}+n^{2}}}\right)
. Attempting to consider another set of
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\log n}}\right)
sub-sets
S_{2,1},\ldots,S_{2,t}
yields no advantage, as other actions that are performed already require a runtime of
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\gamma}}}\right)
. A detailed explanation appears by the end of the proof
Theorem 6.13
.

Appendix B
Multiplicative
\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP

Input:
An undirected graph
G=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E}}\right)
, a positive weight function
w:E\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}
and an integer
\ell\in\mathbb{N}
.

Output:
A matrix
d
which is a
\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP.

Let
\beta_{1},\ldots,\beta_{\ell+1}\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(0,1}}\right)
to be fixed later

Initialize
d
as the edges’ weights and
\infty
otherwise

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell}}\right]

do

\alpha_{i}\leftarrow\msum{\beta_{j}}{j=1}{i}

for

u\in V

do

Compute
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\alpha_{i}}}}\right)

Compute
S_{i}
to be a hitting set to
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\alpha_{i}}}}\right)\mid u\in V}}\right\}

Compute
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{i},n^{\beta_{i+1}}}}\right)

Compute the distances from any
u\in V
to its pivot
p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)

Construct the set of edges
E_{S_{i}}

for

\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x,y}}\right)\in E

do

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]

do

for

v\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(y,S_{i-1},n^{\beta_{i}}}}\right)

do

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),x}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),v}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[v,y}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[x,y}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right),x}}\right]}

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0}}\right\}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]

do

for

s\in S_{i}

do

Invoke SSSP from
s
on
G_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(s}}\right)=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E_{S_{i+1}}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{s}}\right\}\times V}}\right)\cup H\cup R_{i},d}}\right)
and update
d
accordingly

for

u,v\in V

do

for

i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]

do

for

s\in\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{i},n^{\beta_{i+1}}}}\right)

do

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leftarrow\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,s}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[s,v}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]}

for

u,v\in V

do

\mmin{d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right),v}}\right],d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]}{i=0}{\ell+1}

return

d

Algorithm 6

\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP
\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(G=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E}}\right),w}}\right)

For completeness, we provide the
\frac{3\ell+4}{\ell+2}
-APASP algorithm of Akav and Roditty
[
3
]
with a simplifying change whose runtime is
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2+\frac{1}{\ell+2}}}}\right)
instead of the original
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2-\frac{3}{\ell+2}}m^{\frac{2}{\ell+2}}+n^{2}}}\right)
. For the original version, consider
t\in O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\log n}}\right)
sub-sets:
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,n^{\frac{i\cdot\beta_{1}}{t}}}}\right)
and their corresponding hitting-sets
S_{1,i}
, for
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[t}}\right]
. This induces
O\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\log n}}\right)
hitting-sets
S_{1,1},S_{1,2},\ldots,S_{1,t}
and would result in an improved
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(n^{2-\frac{3}{\ell+2}}m^{\frac{2}{\ell+2}}+n^{2}}}\right)
runtime. Similarly to
Appendix
A
, there is no direct advantage in performing additional partitioning of other sets
S_{j}
for
j\geq 2
into
\tilde{O}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\log n}}\right)
sets, as is explained both in
Theorem 6.13
and in
Theorem 7.4
. For a step-by-step construction process of this algorithm, we refer the reader to Akav and Roditty
[
3
]
.

Input:
An undirected weighted graph
G=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(V,E,w}}\right)
, vertices
u,v\in V
, hitting sets
S_{i}
to
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,V,n^{\beta_{1}+\ldots+\beta_{i}}}}\right)
, sets
\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,S_{i},n^{\beta_{i+1}}}}\right)\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(x}}\right)
for all
x\in V
and
i\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[k}}\right]
, an integer
r\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[k}}\right]
and a set of
\beta_{1},\beta_{2}\ldots,\beta_{k+1}\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(0,1}}\right)
.

Output:

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]
.

i\leftarrow r

while

p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)\notin\Gamma\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,S_{i},n^{\beta_{i+1}}}}\right)

do

i\leftarrow i+1

Replace between
u,v

return

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right]+d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[v,p_{i}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right]

Algorithm 7

ThorupZwick-Distance Oracle

Akav and Roditty
[
3
]
denote by
f=f\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v,r}}\right)
the value of the index
i
for which
Algorithm
7
halts. They then proved the following:

Lemma B.1

(
[
3
]
)
.

Let
u,v\in V
and
r\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{0}}\right\}\cup\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\ell+1}}\right]
. If
f-r
is even then
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f-r}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{r}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
; otherwise:
f-r
is odd, and then
\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v,p_{f}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(v}}\right)}}\right)\leq\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f-r}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,p_{r}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u}}\right)}}\right)
.

They make use of this within one of their lemmas which proves an upper-bound on
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]
, similarly to
Lemma
7.3
:

Lemma B.2

(
[
3
]
)
.

d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,a}}\right)
or
d\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[u,v}}\right]\leq\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(u,v}}\right)+2\cdot\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\ell+1}}\right)\cdot\delta\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(b,v}}\right)

Where the above lemma states exactly the samea as does
Lemma
7.3
, yet refers to
Algorithm
6
. The vertices
a,b
are selected in the same way as in
Claim
7.1
.
